headline: Antonelli comes out on top after 4 lead changes in Suzuka
standfirst: Kimi Antonelli won the Japanese Grand Prix for Mercedes, finishing 13.722s ahead of Oscar Piastri, with Charles Leclerc completing the podium after 53 laps of Suzuka.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: Kimi Antonelli lined up first on the grid. Piastri got the better launch and led the field across the line at the end of the opening lap. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Piastri, up 2 places to 1st.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: The lead changed hands 4 times. Laps led: Antonelli (33), Piastri (16) and Russell (4). Antonelli took the lead for good on lap 21. The race was neutralised by 1 safety car period (lap 22–27).

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Antonelli made 1 stop, running medium → hard tyres. The field made 29 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.0s for Hamilton on lap 22. 10 of the top 10 finishers got home with one stop or fewer.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Liam Lawson made up the most ground, climbing 5 places from 14th to 9th. Hadjar went the other way, slipping from 8th to 12th. Timing recorded 218 on-track position changes, 49 of them by Lawson.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Stroll (lap 31) and Bearman (lap 21) failed to finish.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: It stayed dry throughout. Track temperature ranged from 30°C to 37°C, with air at 17–19°C. Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap, a 1:32.432 on lap 49.
